To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the source term balance in the Southern North is strongly dependent on the location in the North Sea and that the newly developed source terms are capable to predict the source term balance reasonably well.

The source terms for the December 2013 North Sea storm are balanced at deep water locations, whereas at inter-mediate depth locations bottom friction plays a role and at shallow water locations bottom friction and depth-limited wave-breaking are of importance.

the newly developed ST6 white-capping formulation is a promising candidate to improve the prediction of wave height in the Southern North-Sea, and that the newly developed source terms for depth limited wave breaking and triads are not yet ready to be used in operational wave prediction models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the verification of the new source terms for wave models in a shallow water environment.
a detailed analysis of the source term budget for a severe North Sea storm, and with the verification of newly developed source terms.
a comparison of different source terms for wave breaking, nonlinear wave-wave interactions and whitecapping.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new source terms perform very well in deep water, but that more work needs to be done in shallow environments to improve the source term balance.
the new ST6 whitecapper performs best in the North Sea.
the new source terms for white-capping and triad interactions perform well in the shallow waters of the southern part of North Sea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the newly developed source terms for wind, whitecapping, four-wave interactions, triad interactions, and depth-limited breaking are all needed to properly describe the source term balance in shallow water environments.
in the deep North Sea the new whitecapping source term performs well and that the new source terms for triad and depth-limited breaking are also promising.
at the inter-mediate and deep water location K13 and North Cormorant the new ST6 whitecapper performs best.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the source term balance is not the same everywhere in the Southern North sea and that the relative importance of the source terms depends on the water depth.
the new whitecapping formulation by Zieger and co-workers is the only whitecapping model that is capable of producing a source term balance in the Southern North sea.
the new deep and shallow water formulations for whitecapping and depth-limited wave-breaking, respectively, are able to reproduce the measured waves in the southern North Sea.
